newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends up on domestic buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends up on domestic buying.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed up on Monday with domestic investors actively building positions on confidence in the short-term stability of the market and due to recent rises in Chinese stocks in Hong Kong, brokers said.
The index ended up 0.972 points or 1.45 percent at 68.129 points on volume of 19.3 million shares worth $8.5 million.
Brokers said market sentiment was strong because there were no signs of political instability after the death of Chinese leader earlier this month.
The gains in the H shares of Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong added confidence to the B share market, they said.
"Domestic investors believe that the recent strong performance of H shares in Hong Kong indicates overseas investors have confidence in China's future," said one broker.
"They believe that after the gains in the H shares, overseas capital will flow into the B share market as well," he added.

"Technical charts have indicated that the B market is ready for a breakthrough," said a second broker. "The near-term trend will depend on whether the B share index can breach the key 69-point resistance level on Tuesday."
On Monday's trading, all 43 B shares in Shangahi traded with 34 up, four flat and five down.
Stationery maker Shanghai Hero was the star performer after it posted strong 1996 results last Saturday, brokers said. The stock rose $0.028 or 6.73 percent to $0.444 on volume of 675,200 shares.
Toy maker Shanghai Haixin traded the most and became the second winner on talk of good results for 1996, brokers said. It added $0.030 or 6.12 percent to $0.520 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index closed higher with fresh liquidity flowing into the market on strong sentiment, brokers said.
It rose 24.033 points or 2.21 percent to 1,111.456 points on volume of 848.4 million shares worth 8.4 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index rose 53.090 points or 1.88 percent to 2,872.488 points.
Shanghai Tyre and Rubber was the biggest gainer on the news that one of its projects had been chosen as a key project for the city in 1997, brokers said.
The stock surged 1.06 yuan to end at a 10-percent limit-up of 11.62 yuan on volume of 1.0 million shares.
